turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey Marcus, you around? I need to vent about the cluster migration.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Always. What happened? Did the new cluster blow up?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Not exactly. I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was ready. I thought the health checks would pass, but they didn't.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh no. So you sent live traffic to a cluster that couldn't serve it?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. For about ten minutes, users got 503s. I felt like an idiot.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: We've all done something like that. Did you roll back?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I flipped DNS back to the old cluster, but the damage was done. The incident report is going to be fun.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: At least you caught it. Next time, wait for the cluster health check before switching DNS. That's the rule we set.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I know, I know. I got impatient. Lesson learned.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, how's the migration going? Did you get the new cluster stable?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Actually, yes. This time I waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS. All green.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice. So you flipped the switch?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yep, traffic moved over without a hitch. Zero errors, zero downtime. It's beautiful.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's the way to do it. See, patience pays off.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I'm just glad I didn't repeat the same mistake. The old cluster is decommissioned now.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. So what's next on your plate?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Honestly, I'm a bit worried about the user auth service. I've been meaning to clean it up.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Priya, did you see the security alert? We had a breach on the user accounts.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: What? No, I just saw the email. How bad is it?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Bad. Someone got into the auth database. They're saying a bunch of accounts are compromised.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Oh god. I think I know why. When I set up the auth service, I stored passwords without hashing. I was in a rush.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: You what? Priya, that's a huge security flaw. No wonder they got in.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I know, I know. I thought we'd fix it later, but later never came. Now we have to notify all those users.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: We need to reset every password, force re-auth, and audit the whole system. This is going to be a nightmare.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I'm so sorry. I should have hashed them from day one. I just didn't think anyone would find out.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Well, they did. Let's focus on damage control. And after this, we're implementing mandatory security reviews for every service.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Agreed. I'll take full responsibility in the postmortem. I just hope we can contain it.
